items.title: Jon Hendricks interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 29, 2000 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: Edison never acknowledged the help he had from Tesla.

ctx.x: That was my son. Well when you look in jazz history there’s a small number comparatively of real innovators. There’s people that build on the innovations. I think that you’re one of those small number of innovators and gosh, you can take a great deal of pride in that.

Well it’s delicate for me because you must be aware of egoism. Egoism — or is it egotism — I don’t know if there’s a “t” in there or not, and I’m an English major I should know. But anyway you must beware of the ego, the overactivity of the ego. Because man nothing is done alone. If it hadn’t been for King Pleasure, for Eddie Jefferson, for Annie Ross’ “Twisted” and “Farmer’s Market” which were done before Lambert, Hendricks & Ross, I would not have had the road sign to point me toward lyricizing orchestral…
